title: Which intent the dialogue policy reads
summary: Dialogue policy reads one intent for the turn: ask, recall, correct, forget, or goodbye, among the labels it keeps. A recall that is not one person source, and a correction or a forget, become the honest miss.
body:
Dialogue layer 4 decides the next move after empathy has stepped the mood and after retrieval has already produced a clause or an honest miss. The heuristic is the policy. An offline count of moves does not change the move. A correction or a forget is not counted. Nothing here writes a file or reads the diary.

The heard line is one intent. The labels kept from the earlier pass are chat, ask, task, vent, and goodbye. A fixed English phrase table then refines recall, forget, and correction. Precedence is correction, then forget, then recall. An unknown label is chat.

Recall speaks a person-memory source or a learned source, or the honest miss when the gathered sources are not one. A correction or a forget becomes that same miss and does not repeat the last sourced clause. Check-ins stay off until the person turns them on. A callback is stored only when remember is granted.
